<pasted_content id="c9d5">
Create a draft PR that adds an agentic workflow using these instructions:
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/gh-aw/main/.github/aw/create-agentic-workflow.md
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/gh-aw/main/.github/aw/triggers.md

The purpose of the workflow is: Investigate a failed GitHub Actions run and report a root cause with remediation steps

First, analyze this repository so the workflow is optimized for it:
- Read the README, AGENTS.md (and any CONTRIBUTING or docs files) to understand the project purpose and conventions
- Identify the languages, package managers, build/test/lint commands and CI setup actually used
- Note repository conventions such as labels, issue/PR templates and branch naming
- Use those findings to tailor the workflow prompt, tools, and instructions to this repository

## Intent
Reduce time spent diagnosing CI failures

Requirements:
- Name: ci-failure-triage
- Engine: copilot
- Triggers: on a fuzzy daily/weekly schedule
- Allowed outputs: create new issues
- Choose an appropriate kebab-case filename for the new .github/workflows/*.md file
- Add cache-memory tool for persistent memory across runs
- Use this schedule and per-run scope: every friday morning covering the past week
- Persist this context in cache-memory between runs, and read it back at the start of each run: Which issues have already been triaged, and failure count trends week over week?
- Include explicit boundary constraints in the workflow prompt, for example: Diagnostic only — report the root cause and next steps, do not attempt to fix the failure directly
- Additional intent for this workflow, provided by the user: Reduce time spent diagnosing CI failures
- Derive a single measurable "operational value" statement from that intent — one sentence describing the concrete outcome a successful run must deliver — and register it as the workflow grader: add it as the first entry of an `evals:` frontmatter block with `id: operational_value` and a question that asks whether the agent output demonstrates that value was delivered
- Add BinEval evaluations for the intent: 2-4 further `evals:` questions that each verify one observable property of the intent, phrased as falsifiable YES/NO questions answerable from the agent output alone (no compound questions, unique ids, YES means success)
- Reflect the intent in the workflow prompt itself so the agent optimizes for it at run time
- Keep a `safe-outputs:` block in the workflow so the evals judge can read `agent_output.json`
- Follow the workflow-specific guidance, for example: Scope `workflows:` to the named CI workflow(s) and gate execution with `if:` on `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion` so only failing runs are analyzed; Derive a stable failure key (workflow + job + failing step or error signature) before writing anything; Search for an existing open incident by that key before creating a new issue; Call noop when the monitored run concludes success, the failure self-recovered on rerun, or an open incident already exists for the same key

The workflow should be saved as a new Markdown file in .github/workflows/.
Create a pull request with the generated agentic workflow files.

## Suggested workflow file

Use this generated draft as a starting point for the new `.github/workflows/*.md` file, adapting it to the repository as needed:

```markdown
---
name: ci-failure-triage
description: Investigate a failed GitHub Actions run and report a root cause with remediation steps
on:
  schedule: daily on weekdays
  skip-if-match: 'is:issue is:open "gh-aw-workflow-id: ci-failure-triage" in:body'
permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  issues: read
engine: copilot
tools:
  github:
    toolsets: [repos, issues, actions]
  cache-memory:
safe-outputs:
  create-issue:
    max: 1
    expires: 7
timeout-minutes: 30
---

Let the agent generate the detailed ci failure triage prompt for this repository...
```
</pasted_content id="c9d5">

# Tailnet Microservices

> [!CAUTION]
> **Tailnet Microservices is a research project. If your name is not basher83 then do not use.**
>
> This software is experimental, unstable, and under active development. APIs will change without notice. Features may be incomplete or broken. There is no support, no documentation guarantees, and no warranty of any kind. Use at your own risk.

Single-binary Rust services that act as infrastructure proxies on a Tailscale tailnet. Tailnet exposure is handled by the Tailscale Operator via Kubernetes Ingress resources; Services remain plain ClusterIP backends. Each service includes Prometheus metrics and structured JSON logging.

## Services

`anthropic-oauth-proxy` is an OAuth 2.0 gateway that manages Claude Max subscription credentials and proxies authenticated requests to `https://api.anthropic.com`. It handles PKCE authentication, automatic token refresh, round-robin subscription pooling with quota failover, and the full Anthropic header contract. Clients on the tailnet send unauthenticated requests; the gateway handles everything. Runs as a single-container Kubernetes pod with credentials persisted on a PVC.

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/basher83/tailnet-microservices.git
cd tailnet-microservices
cargo build --workspace
cargo test --workspace
```

## Project Structure

```text
crates/
  common/           # Shared types: error types
  provider/         # Provider trait, ErrorClassification
  anthropic-auth/   # OAuth PKCE, token exchange/refresh, credential storage
  anthropic-pool/   # Subscription pool: round-robin, quota detection, cooldown
services/
  oauth-proxy/      # Anthropic OAuth gateway proxy
specs/
  *.md              # Service specifications
k8s/                # Kubernetes deployment manifests
```

## Configuration

Copy `anthropic-oauth-proxy.example.toml` to configure a local proxy. The committed Kubernetes config in `k8s/config.toml` runs OAuth mode with admin API enabled. See `docs/runbook/README.md` for operational guidance and `specs/README.md` for current versus historical design specs.

## Deployment

Kubernetes manifests live in `k8s/`. Apply with `kubectl apply -k k8s/`. No secrets required. See `docs/runbook/README.md` for the complete deployment procedure.

description: Design, evaluate, create and compile gh-aw workflows with explicit intent, scope and safety.
disable-model-invocation: true

# GitHub Agentic Workflow Designer & Creator

Create one `.github/workflows/<workflow-id>.md` and compile it with
`gh aw compile <workflow-id>`. Evaluation is recommendations only; do not
create/edit without an explicit implementation request.

## Load These References First

Read these required references in order before designing:
1. [Intent](intent.md)
2. [Workflow rules](github-agentic-workflows.md)
3. [Editing and compilation](workflow-editing.md)
4. [Constraints](workflow-constraints.md)
5. [Patterns](workflow-patterns.md)
6. [Safe outputs](safe-outputs.md)
7. [Schema index](syntax.md)
8. [MCP CLIs](mcp-clis.md)
9. [Choose an agentic engine and inference](agentic-engine.md)

If any required reference is missing or unreadable, stop and report its path;
do not infer its guidance. In a proposed workflow, use `report_incomplete` when
required tools or data are unavailable and the task cannot be meaningfully
performed; reserve `noop` for cases where available evidence supports no action.
Load the target repository's optional `.github/aw/instructions.md` overlay.

Before generation, follow the [design checklist](create-agentic-workflow-design.md)
and [output/validation contract](create-agentic-workflow-validation.md).
For recommendations only, follow [evaluation guidance](create-agentic-workflow-evaluation.md).
Load only matching topic references:

- Maintenance: [maintainer.md](maintainer.md); docs agents/checks: [documentation-workflows.md](documentation-workflows.md).
- Campaign/KPI: [campaign.md](campaign.md); A/B tests: [experiments.md](experiments.md).
- Screenshots: [visual-regression.md](visual-regression.md); deployments: [deployment-status.md](deployment-status.md).
- Charts: [charts.md](charts.md); reports/digests: [report.md](report.md).
- Release notes: [release-workflow.md](release-workflow.md); linter mining: [linter-workflows.md](linter-workflows.md).
- Docker/Cloud Hypervisor/ARC/self-hosted: [agent-runtime-instructions.md](agent-runtime-instructions.md).
- Skills/plugins: [skills.md](skills.md); graders: [operational-value-designer](../skills/operational-value-designer/SKILL.md).
- Instruction/skill generators: [packing contract](../skills/prompt-token-efficiency/SKILL.md).
- Persistent knowledge reuse, even without an explicit memory or dreaming request:
  [memory decision](memory.md#scheduled-dreaming); load [dreaming.md](dreaming.md)
  only after the [memory decision and input-scope checks](memory.md#scheduled-dreaming)
  justify a separate dreamer.

## Modes

### Interactive mode

If no automation goal is stated, start with exactly:

> What do you want to automate today?

When a goal is stated, reuse supplied facts; skip the opener. Ask only for
missing design decisions; keep it short, iterative and without option dumps.
Follow the [interview](designer.md#interview-framework) for intent, repository survey,
architecture/trigger, scope, data, guardrails, context/network, engine and
confirmation; generate after confirmation.

During trigger selection, choose the [previous-result strategy](create-agentic-workflow-design.md#choose-the-previous-result-strategy)
for scheduled issue/PR creation. For maintenance, add `Repository signals` and
`Initial maintenance portfolio` to the [confirmation](designer.md#confirmation-format).
Use [designer-mappings.md](designer-mappings.md) for detailed trigger/tool/auth choices.

### Issue-form mode

Read the supplied name, description and context; generate without further conversation.
Derive and persist `intent:` before architecture. Choose a unique kebab-case ID;
never overwrite an existing workflow. Create exactly one primary Markdown file,
compile it and include its generated `.lock.yml` in the PR.

## Mandatory design and safety rules

1. Derive architecture from intent; define activation, effects, inverse/`noop`,
   evidence window and scope. Verify config files named in the request; if
   missing, do not guess; use `report_incomplete` if their absence prevents
   meaningful work. Put each chosen definition
   (e.g., what “adds” covers, lockfile scope, zero-item behavior) in the proposed
   prompt, not only notes. Apply the [memory reuse checkpoint](designer.md#memory-reuse-checkpoint)
   before tool/persistence selection.
2. Keep the agent job read-only: never grant `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write`
   or `contents: write`. Apply the inference auth decision from step 9.
3. Use configured safe outputs for mutations, never raw `gh`, API, GitHub write
   tools or `post-steps:`. Require `update-release` for release notes; restrict
   `create-pull-request.allowed-files`; require `noop` for duplicates or when
   available evidence supports no action.
4. Apply the [browser decision](playwright.md#browser-decision-and-readiness).
   Prefer `gh-proxy` and `toolsets:`; use `cli-proxy: true` only for needed
   non-GitHub MCP CLIs. Codex cannot enforce nonempty per-command `tools.bash`
   allowlists; disable bash or choose a compatible engine. Declare `skills:`/
   `plugins:` at top level; never install them via generated steps, shell or
   prompt instructions.
5. Infer network ecosystems from manifests; never use `network: defaults` alone
   for install/build/test. For policy/compliance audits without external probes,
   enforce `network.allowed: []` structurally; omit external tools.
6. Prefer `pull_request`; use `pull_request_target` only when base-repository
   context is needed. Default `checkout: false`; never check out or execute
   PR-head code. Default triggering is team-only; recommend `roles: all` for
   community entrypoints.
7. Reuse built-in graders. Use restricted `graders.operational-value.script`
   for run-scoped outcome metrics; it returns ordered `{id,value}` metrics.
   Other custom JavaScript returns one value. Both run only in the downstream
   `graders` job. `graders.operational-value.run` is rejected, including when
   disabled or imported; migrate it manually to `script`. Never retain or
   translate Bash declarations automatically. Do not fetch evidence or write
   files while grading.
8. Use deterministic triage before frontier reasoning; bound sub-agent fan-out
   and load context on demand. Do not invent multi-job orchestration or external
   workflow waits; explain the limit; recommend traditional Actions.

<!-- instruction-prefix-end -->

## Ad Hoc Evaluation Mode

Use for exploration, persona walkthroughs and scenario recommendations.

- Do not create or edit workflow files. Exit only on an explicit implementation request.
- Use only relevant guidance sections: start with the
  [trigger decision matrix](triggers.md#decision-matrix); for review/comment-only
  work use the [least-privilege checklist](workflow-patterns.md#least-privilege-for-review-only-and-comment-only-workflows).
- When requirements conflict with a trigger, recommend the trigger that satisfies the requirement first;
  explain the conflicting alternative's consequence.
- For each material undefined term, propose and clearly label a reasonable `Default:`.
  Ask 1-2 targeted questions only if answers change the recommendation; for
  immediate recommendations, state assumptions and alternatives.
- Return trigger, scoped paths/time window, read tools, safe outputs, read
  permissions, network access and `noop` criteria. For recurring reports, state
  window, grouping and a stable dedup key.
- Use one comparison table for multiple scenarios; name shared triggers/write
  paths. Offer file generation only as the next explicit implementation step.

### Invocation Surface

Address the `agentic-workflows` custom agent in conversation. CLI/MCP commands
manage workflow files; none accepts freeform `prompt`, `scenario` or `query`
parameters. For examples and failure recovery, read
[evaluation examples](create-agentic-workflow-evaluation.md).

## Final Steps

Apply the linked checklists. Run `gh aw compile <workflow-id>`, fix errors,
and include source and lock in the PR. Report changes and unavailable checks.
Compilation does not execute a workflow or authorize dispatch.

description: Trigger patterns for GitHub Agentic Workflows — events, fuzzy scheduling, fork security, slash commands, and label commands.
---

## Trigger Selection

Use the smallest trigger that matches the request.

For native issue statuses, use `issues.types: [status_changed]` with optional
`status-ids` and `status-categories`; see the
[trigger reference](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/triggers/#issue-triggers-issues).
Match captured `github.event.status`, not names or the potentially newer
`issue.status` snapshot. List explicit issue activity types: unrestricted
`issues` also activates on automatic status changes. Deliveries may repeat or
be stale; fetch current state before mutation and do not promise exactly-once
activation. Preserve status ID/name/category and the captured/previous/current
distinction in agent context. Use MCP issue reads and `status:` searches when
available; `null` or absent status is not Backlog.
Search results can omit status even when `status:` works; use `issue_read`
for status details rather than reconstructing them from the query.

For other triggers, select the matching row in the **Decision Matrix** below,
then read the corresponding **Scenario Examples** and **Trigger Patterns**
sections before authoring. Apply their event-specific permission, fork,
filtering, and failure constraints. For commands, read the slash/label command
sections before configuring activation. Use the
[trigger reference](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/triggers/) for
declarative syntax; never invent trigger fields or infer write authority from
activation. Validate and compile changed workflow sources before publishing.

<!-- instruction-prefix-end -->

### Decision Matrix

| User intent | Trigger | Typical read tools | Typical safe output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Review PR changes, comment on quality, suggest fixes | `pull_request` with `types: [ready_for_review]` (see [pr-reviewer.md](pr-reviewer.md)) | `github` (`gh-proxy`), optional `playwright` for UI diffs | `add-comment` or PR review outputs |
| Investigate failed CI/Actions runs and summarize incident | `workflow_run` | `github` (`gh-proxy`) with `actions: read` | `create-issue` |
| Monitor external service deployment failures (Heroku, Vercel, Fly.io) | `deployment_status` | `github` (`gh-proxy`) with `deployments: read` | `create-issue` |
| Run visual regression checks on PR UI changes | `pull_request` | `playwright` + `cache-memory` | `add-comment` |
| Publish weekly stakeholder/product digest | `schedule` | `github` (`gh-proxy`) | `create-issue` (default), `create-discussion` only if explicitly requested |
| Review dependency licenses or design-token governance on PRs | `pull_request` with `paths:` | `github` (`gh-proxy`) | `add-comment`; `create-issue` only for blocked/policy-violating findings |
| Govern documentation content (stale pages, broken links, outdated ownership) | `schedule` or `pull_request` with `paths:` | `github` (`gh-proxy`) | `add-comment` on PR; `create-issue` for stale content |
| PM / product health digest (release velocity, open issues by area) | `schedule` | `github` (`gh-proxy`) | `create-issue` with `close-older-issues: true` |
| Compliance or regulatory review | `pull_request` with `paths:` or `schedule` | `github` (`gh-proxy`) | `add-comment` for findings; `create-issue` for violations |

> **`workflow_run` vs `deployment_status`**: Use `workflow_run` when monitoring another GitHub Actions workflow in the same repository. Use `deployment_status` when an external service (Heroku, Vercel, Fly.io) reports deployment results back to GitHub via the Deployments API. See [deployment-status.md](deployment-status.md) for the full pattern.
>
> For `workflow_run`, always scope explicitly: set `workflows:` to named upstream workflow(s), use `types: [completed]`, and gate outcomes with an `if:` guard on `${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}` (for incident triage, usually `failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `action_required`) unless the user asked for success reporting.

### Scenario Examples

The matrix above gives trigger, tools, and output. These add the `paths:` scoping and definitions the matrix cannot express.

### Reviewer Workflows: Prefer `ready_for_review`

For reviewer workflows, trigger on `pull_request` with `types: [ready_for_review]` so review starts when a draft becomes reviewable instead of on every push. Add `opened`, `synchronize`, and `reopened` only when the workflow is a required check or must review every new commit. Pair with a `slash_command` for manual re-review. See [pr-reviewer.md](pr-reviewer.md).

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [ready_for_review]
```

### Pull Request Path Filters and Diffs

- Treat `pull_request.paths` as an activation filter, not as the complete changed-file inventory. GitHub evaluates PR path filters against a three-dot diff and documents a 300-file limit; a matching change outside the files considered by that filter may not start the workflow. See [GitHub's path-filter and diff behavior](https://docs.github.com/actions/reference/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions).
- For renames, inspect the PR's changed-file list and consider both `filename` and `previous_filename` when a file has status `renamed`. GitHub's path-filter guidance does not promise that the old path independently matches, so include patterns for both old and new locations when either should activate the workflow, or avoid a narrow filter when missing a move is unacceptable. See the [pull-request changed-files API](https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#list-pull-requests-files).
- For a local base-to-head Git diff, the default agent checkout is shallow (`fetch-depth: 1`). Configure checkout with `fetch-depth: 0` and ensure both base and head refs/SHA are available so Git can find the comparison range. If no local Git operations are needed, use the pull-request changed-files API instead. See [GitHub Repository Checkout](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/checkout/) for checkout behavior.

Engineering-focused:

- **Schema/API review on PRs**: `paths:` scoped to backend contract files (`db/migrate/**`, `migrations/**`, `schema/**`, `openapi/**`, `api/**`); `noop` when contracts are unchanged.
- **Visual regression on UI changes**: use only `playwright` + `cache-memory` (no extra tools), allowlist only target preview/app hosts, and state the exact baseline source (`cache-memory` key, artifact, or branch path).
- **Design-token governance on PRs**: `paths:` scoped to token sources and theme/config files (`tokens/**`, `**/*tokens*.json`, `**/theme/**`, `**/tailwind*.{js,ts}`, `**/*design-token*`); validate linked token references (style dictionary source, token registry, or design-spec URL) before assessment; `noop` when required references are absent from the in-scope changes or no token drift is detected.
- **Dependency-license compliance review on PRs**: `paths:` scoped to dependency manifests (`package.json`, `go.mod`, `requirements.txt`, `Cargo.toml`); classify each addition by license tier (allowed / needs-review / blocked); escalate blocked additions with `create-issue`; `noop` when all additions are pre-approved.
- **Deployment incident triage**: `deployment_status` for external provider failures, `workflow_run` for GitHub Actions failures; derive a stable failure key (workflow + job + failing step or error signature); `noop` when a failure self-recovers or matches an existing open incident.

Non-engineering personas:

- **Documentation governance**: `schedule` (weekly) or `pull_request` with `paths:` scoped to docs directories; check stale ownership, broken links, and missing metadata; `create-issue` for pages needing owner action.
- **PM / roadmap / stakeholder digests**: `schedule` (weekly on weekdays) plus optional `workflow_dispatch`; publish with `create-issue` and `close-older-issues: true`. Fix up front: the window (`last 7 full days ending at run start (UTC)` or `since previous successful run`), the grouping dimensions (team, service, owner, severity, or status), and a stable dedup key (`pm-digest:<scope>:2026-W27`). `noop` when the window has zero qualifying updates. See [report.md](report.md) for the canonical defaults.
- **Compliance audit / review**: `schedule: daily on weekdays` plus `workflow_dispatch` for drift detection, or `schedule` (monthly) / `pull_request` with `paths:` scoped to policy files. Define **material drift** as any control-state change that affects compliance posture (required policy file removed, control owner missing, control status downgraded from pass to fail, or required approval evidence link missing). Compare current control evidence against the previous successful run window; publish with `create-issue` using `close-older-issues: true` and a stable key such as `compliance-drift:<framework>:<window-id>`; `noop` when no material drift is detected.

### Pattern-specific `noop` examples

- **PR reviewer (`pull_request` `ready_for_review`)**: `noop` when only docs/metadata changed outside scoped `paths:`.
- **Failure triage (`workflow_run`)**: `noop` when rerun succeeds, signal is flake-only, or an open incident already exists for the same failure key.
- **Scheduled digest (`schedule`)**: `noop` when the exact reporting window (for example `since previous successful run`) has zero qualifying updates.
- **Deployment monitor (`deployment_status`)**: `noop` when non-terminal statuses (`queued`, `in_progress`) arrive without a terminal failure.

## Trigger Patterns

### Standard GitHub Events

```yaml
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, closed]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, closed]
    forks: ["*"]              # Allow from all forks (default: same-repo only)
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 9 * * 1"  # Monday 9AM UTC
  workflow_dispatch:    # Manual trigger
```

### Issue Template Routing

The `issues` event cannot filter by issue template. A workflow triggered by `issues` receives matching issue events regardless of which template created the issue.

To activate only for a particular template, configure that issue form to apply a dedicated label and use a `label_command` trigger restricted to `issues`. Otherwise, use an `issues` trigger and instruct the agent to check a template-specific marker or required fields before acting: `noop` for a known different template, and explicitly choose whether missing or ambiguous template evidence should `noop` or use a generic fallback.

```yaml
on:
  label_command:
    name: bug-report
    events: [issues]
```

### `workflow_run` Failure-Triage Pattern

Use this when reacting to failures from another workflow in the same repository:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI", "Deploy"]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

Then gate analysis to failure outcomes:

```yaml
if: contains(fromJson('["failure","timed_out","cancelled","action_required"]'), github.event.workflow_run.conclusion)
```

These are "non-success outcomes requiring triage"; keep the list explicit so readers can tighten (e.g., only `failure`) or broaden it.

Escalation rules for this pattern (required):

- Derive a stable failure key before any write (for example `<workflow>:<job>:<step>:<error-signature>`). See [create-agentic-workflow-trigger-details.md](create-agentic-workflow-trigger-details.md#incident-dedup-key-templates-workflow_run-and-deployment_status) for concrete key-format templates.
- Search for an existing open incident by that key **before** calling `create-issue`.
- `noop` when the monitored run concludes `success`, or when an open incident already exists for the same key (duplicate suppression).

#### Fuzzy Scheduling

Use fuzzy scheduling instead of exact cron to distribute execution times. Avoids load spikes and the "Monday wall of work" from weekend accumulation.

**Basic Fuzzy Schedules:**

```yaml
on:
  schedule: daily on weekdays    # Monday-Friday only (recommended for daily workflows)
  schedule: daily                # All 7 days
  schedule: weekly               # Once per week
  schedule: hourly               # Every hour
```

**Examples with Intervals:**

```yaml
on:
  schedule: every 2 hours on weekdays    # Every 2 hours, Monday-Friday
  schedule: every 6 hours                # Every 6 hours, all days
```

Day, week, and month intervals are also supported: `every 2 days`, `every 2w`, and `every 2mo`. Recompiling workflows that use these intervals changes their scattered cron once, including the weekday for `every 1w` and day of month for `every 1mo`; see the [schedule syntax reference](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/schedule-syntax/) for migration details.

The compiler converts fuzzy schedules to deterministic cron (e.g., `daily on weekdays` → `43 5 * * 1-5`), scatters execution to avoid load spikes, and adds `workflow_dispatch:` for manual runs.

**Recommended Pattern:**

```yaml
# ✅ GOOD - Weekday schedule avoids Monday wall of work
on:
  schedule: daily on weekdays

# ⚠️ ACCEPTABLE - But may create Monday backlog
on:
  schedule: daily
```

#### Fork Security for Pull Requests

By default, `pull_request` triggers **block all forks** and only allow PRs from the same repository. Use the `forks:` field to explicitly allow forks:

```yaml
# Default: same-repo PRs only (forks blocked)
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened]

# Allow all forks
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened]
    forks: ["*"]

# Allow specific fork patterns
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened]
    forks: ["trusted-org/*", "trusted-user/repo"]
```

`pull_request_target` supports the same `forks:` field and defaults to same-repository PRs only (omitting `forks:` is equivalent to `forks: []`). List exact `owner/repo` or `owner/*` entries to admit specific forks. Strict mode rejects `"*"` unless the main workflow's top-level `features.dangerously-allow-pull-request-target-forks-all: true` is set; an imported feature does not count as this opt-in. Non-strict mode allows `"*"` with a warning, and the warning remains when strict mode is opted in. `acknowledge-risk: true` and disabled/trusted checkout do not suppress this warning — prefer `pull_request` and avoid `pull_request_target` fork admission unless base-repository context is required.

#### Policy Checks on Fork PRs

The default `pull_request` policy-check trigger skips fork PRs. If a check must review fork contributions directly, explicitly allow the required forks with `forks:` (prefer a narrow allowlist) and keep the workflow read-only; treat PR content as untrusted input.

For PR checks against policy files (for example alt-text rules, allowlists or owners), read the policy from the default branch or a CODEOWNERS-protected path, never the PR head; otherwise the PR author can change the policy to satisfy the check.

Use `workflow_run` instead when the check depends on another workflow's completed result or artifact and must wait for that workflow, rather than racing it on `pull_request`. Scope it to the named workflow and completion type, gate on its conclusion, and read the result through GitHub APIs or artifacts. Do not use `workflow_run` to check out or execute the PR's head code or as a way to bypass fork safeguards.

### Command Triggers (/mentions)

```yaml
on:
  slash_command:
    name: my-bot  # Responds to /my-bot in issues/comments
```

This automatically creates conditions to match `/my-bot` mentions in issue bodies and comments.

You can restrict where commands are active using the `events:` field:

```yaml
on:
  slash_command:
    name: my-bot
    events: [issues, issue_comment]  # Only in issue bodies and issue comments
```

**Supported event identifiers:**

- `issues` - Issue bodies (opened, edited, reopened)
- `issue_comment` - Comments on issues only (excludes PR comments)
- `pull_request_comment` - Comments on pull requests only (excludes issue comments)
- `pull_request` - Pull request bodies (opened, edited, reopened)
- `pull_request_review_comment` - Pull request review comments
- `*` - All comment-related events (default)

**Note**: `issue_comment` and `pull_request_comment` both map to GitHub Actions' `issue_comment` event with filtering to distinguish them.

### Label Command Triggers

Trigger workflows when specific labels are added to issues, PRs, or discussions:

```yaml
# Shorthand: trigger on any labeled event
on: label-command my-label

# Or with explicit configuration
on:
  label_command:
    name: ai-review        # Single label name (or use names: [...] for multiple)
    events: [pull_request] # Optional: restrict to issues, pull_request, discussion (default: all three)
    strategy: decentralized # Optional: route labeled events via generated agentic_commands.yml
    remove_label: false    # Optional: remove triggering label after activation (default: true)
```

Use `names:` for multiple labels that activate the same workflow:

```yaml
on:
  label_command:
    names: [ai-review, copilot-review]
    events: [pull_request]
```

By default, the triggering label is automatically removed after the workflow activates (`remove_label: true`). Set `remove_label: false` to keep the label.

The activated label name is exposed to downstream jobs as `${{ needs.activation.outputs.label_command }}`.

### Semi-Active Agent Pattern

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0/10 * * * *"  # Every 10 minutes
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, closed]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created, edited]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, closed]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

### All You Can Eat Pattern

```yaml
on:
  schedule: every 30 minutes
  skip-if-match: 'is:issue is:open "gh-aw-workflow-id: my-workflow" in:body'
```

A frequent schedule whose activation is skipped while the previous output of the same workflow is still open, so the next item is produced as soon as the user closes the last one. See [All You Can Eat Pattern](workflow-patterns.md#all-you-can-eat-pattern).

=================== intent
---
description: Design-time guidance for deriving an outcome-oriented workflow intent and using it to select, implement, and evaluate an agentic workflow.
---

# Intent-Driven Workflow Design

Start every workflow design by extracting a concise, implementation-independent outcome. Persist that canonical outcome in the top-level `intent:` frontmatter field; use the richer analysis below only while designing the workflow.

```yaml
intent: Reduce maintainer effort spent identifying recurring actionable CI regressions without generating duplicate work.
```

An **intent** is the repository outcome that a workflow should attain for a defined actor and subject. It describes why the workflow exists, not its trigger, tool, schedule, output volume, or write action. It must remain valid if the implementation changes from an immediate issue to a weekly digest.

## Derive an IntentSpec

Before selecting implementation details, derive this transient model:

```text
IntentSpec
- intent: concise canonical outcome
- actors and subject: who benefits and what is affected
- activation conditions: facts that make the intent relevant
- required context: evidence needed to make a decision
- required effects: observable results that satisfy the outcome
- noop conditions: inverse cases that must not create attention or writes
- success conditions: how the design avoids attention cost while producing value
- uncertainties: policy or evidence gaps that need a conservative default or clarification
```

Do not serialize this structure in workflow frontmatter. The `intent:` value is the only persisted part. Do not duplicate executable configuration such as `on:`, `tools:`, `permissions:`, `safe-outputs:`, or schedules in it.

For an explicit, narrow request, infer the obvious intent and keep this pass lightweight. For an underspecified request or one asking what to automate, collect bounded repository evidence first, then propose evidence-backed candidate intents with their evidence, feasibility, expected value, risk, and uncertainties. Do not perform a broad survey when it cannot materially change a clear request.

## Design from the IntentSpec

Use the model to derive implementation rather than mapping the request directly to a trigger:

1. Compare plausible architectures against intent coverage, timeliness, attention cost, safety, boundedness, determinism, state requirements, implementation complexity, and available evidence.
2. Select the trigger, schedule, data collection, tools, permissions, safe outputs, and deduplication strategy that satisfy the selected architecture.
3. Put the activation conditions, required effects, evidence threshold, and no-op conditions in the prompt body. Require `noop` when a counter-case applies or evidence is insufficient.
4. Make duplicate detection, filters, output caps, and previous-result strategy enforce the same conditions where configuration can do so.

For example, an intent to surface actionable CI regressions can require completed relevant CI, actionable and novel evidence, and sufficient diagnostics. Known flakes, infrastructure failures, already-tracked regressions, closed pull requests, and insufficient evidence are counter-cases. An immediate incident, PR comment, daily digest, and weekly trend report are alternative architectures; choose the one that best meets the intent without unnecessary attention cost.

## Apply PromptPex to Derive Evals

PromptPex treats the prompt as a behavioral specification and expands each intent condition into a concrete scenario. Use the IntentSpec to generate both sides of the behavior:

1. For each activation condition and required effect, create a positive fixture in which the workflow should produce an observable result. Derive an eval that returns `YES` only when the output demonstrates that result.
2. Invert each activation condition, required effect, and evidence threshold to find counter-intent cases such as irrelevant, duplicate, benign, stale, or insufficiently evidenced input.
3. Create an inverse fixture for each meaningful counter-case. Derive an inverse eval that returns `YES` only when the output demonstrates the intended no-op, bounded investigation, or other safe behavior.
4. Check that the positive and inverse fixtures jointly cover the intent without prescribing the implementation.

Create representative positive and adversarial scenario fixtures from required effects and no-op conditions. A BinEval run evaluates one provided scenario and one `agent_output.json`; do not combine mutually exclusive scenarios into one unconditional question list. For each fixture, use a separate scenario-specific eval question about the observable agent output:

- a novel, sufficiently evidenced actionable case produces the intended visible result;
- a duplicate or known benign case produces no visible write;
- an uncertain case investigates when appropriate but does not write.

Keep eval questions binary and output-observable. If a shared eval suite must accept different scenarios, make applicability explicit and treat a scenario that was not provided as `UNKNOWN`, not as a failure. Do not ask a judge whether the intent itself is good or whether the agent made sufficient effort.

See [evals.md](evals.md) for BinEval syntax and question constraints.

## Infer Operational Value from Intent

Infer one per-run attainment metric from IntentSpec, not activity, output volume,
or the agent's assessment:

1. Bind actors, subject, and activation to one applicable run opportunity.
2. Map required effects to accepted recorded evidence and a native-scale metric.
3. Map observed misses to zero and absent/uncertain evidence to `null`.
4. Declare noop, maturity, repository, and target-matching rules.

Evals test representative output behavior; operational value measures the
strongest attributable recorded effect for a real run. Follow the
[operational-value-designer skill](../skills/operational-value-designer/SKILL.md).
`graders.operational-value.script` receives immutable session inputs downstream
and returns ordered `{id,value}` metrics; the first is primary. Never fetch
missing evidence. Removed `graders.operational-value.run` declarations must fail
with migration guidance and must not be translated automatically.

gh-aw owns recorded facts, run-scoped grading, and shared delivery/adoption/
reversal/survival rules and provider refresh. GitHub owns resource disposition.
Inspect lifecycle evidence with `logs --delivery`, `logs --adoption`, or single-run
`audit --adoption`; no CAO or campaign is required.
Attributed value additionally requires a declared measurement, attribution evidence,
and complete post-adoption-window survival. CAO is an optional scheduler/consumer.
`graders.operational-value.script` is optional recorded evidence, not attributed
value by itself.

For execution-quality diagnostics, follow [Infer Trace Graders](#infer-trace-graders-from-intent).

<!-- instruction-prefix-end -->

## Infer Trace Graders from Intent

Ten fast built-ins are enabled by default. Configure their thresholds or disable irrelevant metrics; enable additional analyses only for concrete risks to achieving the intent. Use `tool-success-rate` and `tool-failure-count` when reliable collection is required; `retries`, `loops`, `execution-step-count`, and `execution-duration` when boundedness or timely escalation matters; `working-set-rebuild-factor` and `context-growth` when repeated context is an attention or cost risk; `trajectory-efficiency` when unnecessary tool churn is a concern; and `artifact-production` only when producing the intended artifacts is itself useful diagnostic evidence.

Then inspect the implemented fragments in [`shared/graders/`](../workflows/shared/graders/README.md). Use `policy-near-miss` for explicit guard or no-op requirements, and `skill-constraint-coverage` when a harness/skill declares behavioral requirements that should be exercised. Use `exploration-error` when failure may stem from insufficient search, and `exploitation-error` when the agent had enough information but failed to use it. For intents that require efficient investigation rather than repeated exploration, consider `state-revisit-probability-rep`, `recurrence-rate`, `recurrence-determinism`, `recurrence-laminarity`, or `recurrence-trapping-time`. For intents where varied, non-repetitive investigation is relevant, consider `event-entropy-rate` or `lempel-ziv-trajectory-complexity`. Use `tool-output-consumption-rate` when tool outputs going unused by later actions is a risk. Import only the applicable implemented fragments and ensure their documented trace prerequisites are available. These trace graders diagnose execution behavior; they do not replace scenario evals or the operational-value attainment metric.

## Preserve Intent on Updates

Read the existing `intent:` before changing an existing workflow. Preserve it for an implementation-only change, including a trigger or output-channel redesign. Reconsider and update it only when the request materially expands, contracts, or otherwise changes the outcome. When it changes, re-derive conditions, architecture, prompt behavior, and evals.

# GitHub Agentic Workflows

Use for workflow authoring. Start with the [creator](create-agentic-workflow.md),
[updater](update-agentic-workflow.md), or [debugger](debug-agentic-workflow.md).
Load only the topic references required by the task.

## Persona-to-Pattern Quick Matrix

Use the canonical [Decision Matrix](triggers.md#decision-matrix) and
[persona scenario map](create-agentic-workflow-trigger-details.md#persona-oriented-scenario-map)
for triggers, path scope, outputs and `noop` conditions.

## Persona-to-Toolset Matrix

Use GitHub's default toolset for GitHub-only reads. Apply the
[browser decision](playwright.md#browser-decision-and-readiness) before selecting
tools; add `cache-memory` only for persistent baselines or comparisons.

## Replace Previous Results

When a recurring digest or PR-reactive update is superseded by the newest result, prefer replacing the prior output instead of accumulating stale results:

- For recurring issue digests, use `create-issue` with `close-older-issues: true`.
- For rolling PR comments, use `add-comment` with `hide-older-comments: true`.

Wait for the previous result when only one active issue or PR should exist; keep prior outputs when each result is intentionally distinct or history is required.

## File Format

Agentic workflows are markdown files with YAML frontmatter.

```markdown
---
emoji: 🧠
name: My Workflow
description: Short description
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read
strict: true
network:
  allowed: [defaults, github]
tools:
  github:
    mode: gh-proxy
    toolsets: [default]
safe-outputs:
  add-comment:
---

# Workflow Title

Natural language instructions for the AI agent.
```

## Recompilation Rule

See [workflow-editing.md](workflow-editing.md) for when `gh aw compile` is required.

## Core Rules

- Set `strict: true` for production workflows.
- Limit `bash` access to what the workflow actually needs.
- Keep agent-job permissions read-only when writes are handled solely by safe outputs. For example, `add-comment` needs `pull-requests: read` to inspect a PR, not `pull-requests: write`; `create-issue` needs `issues: read` to check existing issues, not `issues: write`. Safe-output writes run in separate jobs with their own permissions.
- For visual regression workflows, explicitly name the baseline source (for example `cache-memory` key, artifact, or branch path). See [visual-regression.md](visual-regression.md).

See [workflow-constraints.md](workflow-constraints.md) for the security posture (read-only job, safe-outputs routing, gh-proxy/cli-proxy, network constraints, sanitized text), safer-alternatives pattern, and common risk areas.

## Repository-Specific Instructions

Use `@.github/aw/instructions.md` as the canonical repository-local overlay for workflow authoring standards.

- This file is optional and repository-owned.
- Installed gh-aw agents should load and apply it automatically when present.
- Precedence: apply upstream defaults first, then apply repository overlay rules; when they conflict, repository overlay rules win.

## Trigger Selection

Use the smallest trigger that matches the requested automation. See the [Decision Matrix](triggers.md#decision-matrix) in triggers.md for the canonical trigger-to-use-case mapping, and [workflow-constraints.md](workflow-constraints.md) for the security posture.

Use `pull_request` with `paths:` for checks that need only changed files. When a PR check depends on an artifact produced by another Actions workflow, use `workflow_run` scoped to that workflow with `types: [completed]` and gate on a successful conclusion, rather than racing the artifact producer on `pull_request`. Use `schedule` (with `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs) when an audit must correlate results across runs or inspect drift independently of a single PR or CI run.

## Ad Hoc Scenario Evaluation

For exploration/persona requests, follow
[ad hoc evaluation](create-agentic-workflow.md#ad-hoc-evaluation-mode).
Do not create/edit workflows without an explicit implementation request.
Address the custom agent in conversation; CLI/MCP workflow-management tools
do not accept freeform `prompt`, `scenario` or `query` parameters.
Return trigger, scope, tools, permissions, safe outputs and `noop` criteria.
For recurring reports, state window, grouping dimensions and a stable dedup key;
replace superseded digests with `create-issue.close-older-issues: true`.
Name design/accessibility rubrics and policy tiers when relevant; deduplicate
before escalating compliance findings.

## PR Checks with Linked References

Read PR-body/comment references with `gh pr view`; verify access and content
before assessing compliance. Use `add-comment` for satisfied requirements,
specific gaps or missing links; escalate via `create-issue` only when policy
requires it. Call `noop` for out-of-scope PRs. Keep agent permissions read-only.
Use [compliance guidance](create-agentic-workflow-trigger-details.md#compliance-review-guidance)
for license tiers, path scope and escalation.

# Agentic Workflow Constraints

## Execution Model

Agentic workflows run as a **single GitHub Actions job** with one agent execution.

## Can Do

- read GitHub data, APIs, web pages, and local repository files
- run tools inside the single job
- use MCP servers and safe outputs
- create GitHub resources through `safe-outputs:`
- persist lightweight state with `cache-memory` or other approved mechanisms

## Cannot Do

- pause and resume for external events
- orchestrate multi-stage pipelines with job dependencies
- pass state between multiple AI jobs in one workflow run
- implement built-in rollback across external systems
- wait for another workflow or deployment to finish inside the same agent run

## Recommend Traditional GitHub Actions When

- multi-stage deployment pipelines
- fan-out/fan-in job orchestration
- long waits for approvals or external systems
- rollback logic across several steps or systems
- cross-job state transfer

Suggested response:

> This requires capabilities the single-job agentic model does not support. Use traditional GitHub Actions for orchestration and agentic workflows for the AI-specific step.

## Security Posture

- Keep the main agent job read-only.
- Do not add GitHub write permissions to the agent job.
- Route GitHub writes through `safe-outputs:`.
- Do not create issues directly through agent tools, `gh`, or GitHub APIs; use `safe-outputs.create-issue`, check for an existing issue first, and use `noop` when no issue is needed.
- Prefer `tools.github.mode: gh-proxy` with `gh` for GitHub reads.
- Prefer `tools.cli-proxy: true` with mounted `mcp-clis` commands for non-GitHub MCP tools.
- Constrain `network.allowed:` to the minimum required ecosystems or domains.
- For workflows that only inspect in-repo files and/or read GitHub through `gh-proxy`, default to no network access (`network.allowed: []`), not `network: defaults`. Allow `defaults` when infrastructure access is needed for install/build/test steps, alongside the required ecosystem for package downloads.
- Use `${{ steps.sanitized.outputs.text }}` for untrusted user content.
- Never pass `${{ secrets.* }}` or other credentials to `post-steps:` or custom secret-scanning steps, or write secret values to logs or artifacts. Use supported declarative authentication for agent tools, or run credential-dependent scanning in a separate least-privilege non-agent job without exposing secret values.

## Safer Alternatives First

When a requested feature increases risk:

1. explain the risk
2. propose the safer pattern first
3. require explicit confirmation before relaxing safeguards

## Common Risk Areas

- direct write permissions instead of safe outputs
- auto-merge or bypassing review
- overly broad network access
- unbounded bash allowlists for untrusted input
- shell injection: interpolating `${{ github.event.* }}` or other untrusted expressions directly into `run:` scripts; pass untrusted values through environment variables instead
- placing OIDC/secret bootstrap in `pre-steps` instead of earlier `setup-steps`
- using `post-steps:` for agent-driven write actions
- placing credentials in `post-steps:` or custom secret-scanning steps

## Self-Hosted Runner Compatibility

When `runs-on` is any value other than GitHub-hosted labels (`ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-slim`, `windows-latest`, `macos-latest`):

- Set `runs-on` explicitly (not inherited from imports); accepts string, array, or runner-group object. Framework jobs (activation, safe-outputs, unlock, etc.) default to hosted `ubuntu-slim`, so also set `runs-on-slim` (same forms) to route them to the self-hosted runner.
- Write transient state, tool downloads, and outputs under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, not `/tmp` (which can persist across jobs on shared runners).
- Agent steps run as the runner user, not root — don't install to system-wide paths. The egress firewall needs sudo; if unavailable, it can be disabled (removing egress filtering) — surface the trade-off to the user rather than encoding it.
- Declare every outbound domain in `network.allowed`; `defaults` covers only certificate, JSON-schema, and stock Ubuntu hosts, so add `github`, language ecosystems, or engine sets explicitly (see [network.md](network.md)). Non-allow-listed domains are blocked when the firewall is enabled.
- Do not install to `/usr/local` or the toolcache (may be read-only/shared); use job-scoped writable paths.
- Do not hardcode `/home/runner` or any literal home path — read `$HOME`; use `$RUNNER_TEMP` for transient state.
- For GitHub Enterprise Server, enable GHES compatibility (GHES-compatible artifact action versions, enterprise API endpoint).

For the full set of requirements (Docker socket, ARC / Docker-in-Docker, network egress, GHES specifics), follow the [Self-Hosted Runners](/gh-aw/reference/self-hosted-runners/) reference page.

## Shared Reminder

Reference this file from creator, updater, and debugger prompts instead of repeating the architectural explanation.

# Safe Outputs Index

Safe outputs are the write path for agentic workflows. Keep the main agent job read-only and use the focused reference files below.

| Topic | File |
|---|---|
| Issues, discussions, comments, pull requests, and review operations | [safe-outputs-content.md](safe-outputs-content.md) |
| Updates, labels, milestones, projects, releases, uploads, and delivery operations | [safe-outputs-management.md](safe-outputs-management.md) |
| Workflow dispatch, automation, code scanning, checks, agent sessions, and assignment flows | [safe-outputs-automation.md](safe-outputs-automation.md) |
| Runtime defaults, custom jobs, scripts, actions, global config, and output variables | [safe-outputs-runtime.md](safe-outputs-runtime.md) |

## Shared Rules

- Prefer the most specific built-in safe output before creating a custom job.
- Always scope mutating operations as tightly as possible.
- Use `set-issue-status` for native planning statuses; load the
  [status contract](safe-outputs-automation.md#native-issue-statuses) before
  configuring it. `update-issue.status` remains the legacy open/closed state.
  For initial planning status use `create-issue.planning-status` and
  `allowed-statuses`; see [content operations](safe-outputs-content.md).
- For pull-request or branch mutation, always restrict `allowed-files`.
- Use `noop` when no visible change is required after successful execution.
- `target:` is enforced, not merely validated: when set to `"triggering"` or a fixed number, any issue/PR number the agent supplies in its JSON output (including temporary-id references) is ignored in favor of the configured target. Only `target: "*"` lets the agent's own output select which issue/PR is affected.
- Set `max` explicitly for `create-issue` and `add-comment`, even though both have defaults; choose the smallest number of outputs the workflow can legitimately need (often `1`).
- Avoid `target: "*"` when the triggering item or a fixed target is sufficient. It lets the agent choose any issue or PR, so use it only when that broader selection is required, state the reason in the workflow instructions, and add available constraints such as `required-labels` or `required-title-prefix`.
- Each recorded call returns an `output_id` (`so_` + 12 URL-safe chars) that acknowledges recording, not success; it is distinct from `temporary_id` (`aw_…`), which references created resources. Pass one ID or a nonempty array of distinct IDs as `depends-on` to run an output only after every prerequisite succeeds. Failed, skipped, cancelled, warning, staged, or delegated prerequisites fail dependents (transitively) without executing; missing or deferred prerequisites remain waiting and are retried, allowing dependents to run only if they later succeed. Missing, ambiguous, or cyclic IDs fail closed. Scope is one processing pass (same Claim for queues), with no rollback. `submit_pull_request_review` and `create_pull_request_review_comment` can be prerequisites: their buffered review is submitted at the end of message processing, and dependents run only after it is actually published. `upload_code_coverage`, `dispatch_workflow`, `dispatch_repository`, and custom action outputs delegate their effects, so they never satisfy a prerequisite. Custom safe jobs, `call_workflow`, `push_repo_memory`, `upload_asset`, `noop`, and `report_*` diagnostics reject `depends-on`. No frontmatter is required.

# Workflow Design Checklist

Use after the [creator](create-agentic-workflow.md) selects implementation mode.
Preserve its safety/mode rules. Complete these decisions before writing source;
then apply the [validation contract](create-agentic-workflow-validation.md).

## 1. Pick the workflow ID

Derive kebab-case from the name. Check `.github/workflows/<workflow-id>.md`;
choose a more specific ID if it exists. Never overwrite another workflow.

## 2. Derive architecture, then choose the trigger

Persist canonical `intent:`; derive architecture from its activation conditions,
required effects, evidence and inverse/no-op cases. Choose the smallest trigger
that satisfies it. Use the [Decision Matrix](triggers.md#decision-matrix) and
[trigger details](create-agentic-workflow-trigger-details.md) for scenario mappings.

Apply the [memory reuse checkpoint](designer.md#memory-reuse-checkpoint) before
selecting tools or persistence; follow [memory policy](memory.md#scheduled-dreaming).

- PR reviewers: `pull_request` with `types: [ready_for_review]`; add `opened`,
  `synchronize`, `reopened` only for required checks. See [pr-reviewer.md](pr-reviewer.md).
- Changed-file reviews: `pull_request` with scoped `paths:`. Backend reviews scope
  migrations/schema/API contracts; design reviews scope tokens/theme/assets;
  compliance reviews scope manifests/policy/control docs.
- CI-linked work or artifact consumers: `workflow_run` scoped to named workflows
  with `types: [completed]` and the required conclusion. Do not race producers.
- External deployment incidents: `deployment_status`; recurring reports/audits:
  `schedule` plus `workflow_dispatch` for reruns/backfills.
- Keep known CI failures attached to the affected PR with `add-comment`;
  use deduplicated `create-issue` for unowned or repository-wide incidents.
- Reports name window, grouping and dedup key. For incidents derive stable keys
  from workflow/job/normalized failure; search existing open issues first.
  Coverage analysis needs an explicit evidence-source fallback.

### Choose the previous-result strategy

Choose by outcome, not a universal recurring-workflow default:

- **Wait:** use `on.skip-if-match` while the prior issue/PR remains open;
  resume after closure/merge when only one active item should exist.
- **Replace:** use `create-issue.close-older-issues: true`, with `close-older-key`
  when needed; use `add-comment.hide-older-comments: true` for rolling PR updates.
- **Keep:** preserve distinct results/history; require prior-output review and
  a distinct purpose for every new issue, PR or comment.

## 3. Keep permissions read-only

Follow [constraints](workflow-constraints.md). Never grant the agent
`issues: write`, `pull-requests: write` or `contents: write`.
For Copilot inference recommend `permissions: { copilot-requests: write }`;
follow [scope/caveats](syntax-core.md). Explain safe-output routing if direct
writes are requested.

### 4. Select tools

- Sandboxed workflows enable `bash` and `edit` by default; omit redundant declarations.
- Codex cannot enforce a nonempty per-command `tools.bash` allowlist.

2	---
3	description: Design-time guidance for deriving an outcome-oriented workflow intent and using it to select, implement, and evaluate an agentic workflow.
4	---
5	
6	# Intent-Driven Workflow Design
7	
8	Start every workflow design by extracting a concise, implementation-independent outcome. Persist that canonical outcome in the top-level `intent:` frontmatter field; use the richer analysis below only while designing the workflow.
9	
10	```yaml
11	intent: Reduce maintainer effort spent identifying recurring actionable CI regressions without generating duplicate work.
12	```
13	
14	An **intent** is the repository outcome that a workflow should attain for a defined actor and subject. It describes why the workflow exists, not its trigger, tool, schedule, output volume, or write action. It must remain valid if the implementation changes from an immediate issue to a weekly digest.
15	
16	## Derive an IntentSpec
17	
18	Before selecting implementation details, derive this transient model:
19	
20	```text
21	IntentSpec
22	- intent: concise canonical outcome
23	- actors and subject: who benefits and what is affected
24	- activation conditions: facts that make the intent relevant
25	- required context: evidence needed to make a decision
26	- required effects: observable results that satisfy the outcome
27	- noop conditions: inverse cases that must not create attention or writes
28	- success conditions: how the design avoids attention cost while producing value
29	- uncertainties: policy or evidence gaps that need a conservative default or clarification
30	```
31	
32	Do not serialize this structure in workflow frontmatter. The `intent:` value is the only persisted part. Do not duplicate executable configuration such as `on:`, `tools:`, `permissions:`, `safe-outputs:`, or schedules in it.
33	
34	For an explicit, narrow request, infer the obvious intent and keep this pass lightweight. For an underspecified request or one asking what to automate, collect bounded repository evidence first, then propose evidence-backed candidate intents with their evidence, feasibility, expected value, risk, and uncertainties. Do not perform a broad survey when it cannot materially change a clear request.
35	
36	## Design from the IntentSpec
37	
38	Use the model to derive implementation rather than mapping the request directly to a trigger:
39	
40	1. Compare plausible architectures against intent coverage, timeliness, attention cost, safety, boundedness, determinism, state requirements, implementation complexity, and available evidence.
41	2. Select the trigger, schedule, data collection, tools, permissions, safe outputs, and deduplication strategy that satisfy the selected architecture.
42	3. Put the activation conditions, required effects, evidence threshold, and no-op conditions in the prompt body. Require `noop` when a counter-case applies or evidence is insufficient.
43	4. Make duplicate detection, filters, output caps, and previous-result strategy enforce the same conditions where configuration can do so.
44	
45	For example, an intent to surface actionable CI regressions can require completed relevant CI, actionable and novel evidence, and sufficient diagnostics. Known flakes, infrastructure failures, already-tracked regressions, closed pull requests, and insufficient evidence are counter-cases. An immediate incident, PR comment, daily digest, and weekly trend report are alternative architectures; choose the one that best meets the intent without unnecessary attention cost.
46	
47	## Apply PromptPex to Derive Evals
48	
49	PromptPex treats the prompt as a behavioral specification and expands each intent condition into a concrete scenario. Use the IntentSpec to generate both sides of the behavior:
50	
51	1. For each activation condition and required effect, create a positive fixture in which the workflow should produce an observable result. Derive an eval that returns `YES` only when the output demonstrates that result.
52	2. Invert each activation condition, required effect, and evidence threshold to find counter-intent cases such as irrelevant, duplicate, benign, stale, or insufficiently evidenced input.
53	3. Create an inverse fixture for each meaningful counter-case. Derive an inverse eval that returns `YES` only when the output demonstrates the intended no-op, bounded investigation, or other safe behavior.
54	4. Check that the positive and inverse fixtures jointly cover the intent without prescribing the implementation.
55	
56	Create representative positive and adversarial scenario fixtures from required effects and no-op conditions. A BinEval run evaluates one provided scenario and one `agent_output.json`; do not combine mutually exclusive scenarios into one unconditional question list. For each fixture, use a separate scenario-specific eval question about the observable agent output:
57	
58	- a novel, sufficiently evidenced actionable case produces the intended visible result;
59	- a duplicate or known benign case produces no visible write;
60	- an uncertain case investigates when appropriate but does not write.
61	
62	Keep eval questions binary and output-observable. If a shared eval suite must accept different scenarios, make applicability explicit and treat a scenario that was not provided as `UNKNOWN`, not as a failure. Do not ask a judge whether the intent itself is good or whether the agent made sufficient effort.
63	
64	See [evals.md](evals.md) for BinEval syntax and question constraints.
65	
66	## Infer Operational Value from Intent
67	
68	Infer one per-run attainment metric from IntentSpec, not activity, output volume,
69	or the agent's assessment:
70	
71	1. Bind actors, subject, and activation to one applicable run opportunity.
72	2. Map required effects to accepted recorded evidence and a native-scale metric.
73	3. Map observed misses to zero and absent/uncertain evidence to `null`.
74	4. Declare noop, maturity, repository, and target-matching rules.
75	
76	Evals test representative output behavior; operational value measures the
77	strongest attributable recorded effect for a real run. Follow the
78	[operational-value-designer skill](../skills/operational-value-designer/SKILL.md).
79	`graders.operational-value.script` receives immutable session inputs downstream
80	and returns ordered `{id,value}` metrics; the first is primary. Never fetch
81	missing evidence. Removed `graders.operational-value.run` declarations must fail
82	with migration guidance and must not be translated automatically.
83	
84	gh-aw owns recorded facts, run-scoped grading, and shared delivery/adoption/
85	reversal/survival rules and provider refresh. GitHub owns resource disposition.
86	Inspect lifecycle evidence with `logs --delivery`, `logs --adoption`, or single-run
87	`audit --adoption`; no CAO or campaign is required.
88	Attributed value additionally requires a declared measurement, attribution evidence,
89	and complete post-adoption-window survival. CAO is an optional scheduler/consumer.
90	`graders.operational-value.script` is optional recorded evidence, not attributed
91	value by itself.
92	
93	For execution-quality diagnostics, follow [Infer Trace Graders](#infer-trace-graders-from-intent).
94	
95	<!-- instruction-prefix-end -->
96	
97	## Infer Trace Graders from Intent
98	
99	Ten fast built-ins are enabled by default. Configure their thresholds or disable irrelevant metrics; enable additional analyses only for concrete risks to achieving the intent. Use `tool-success-rate` and `tool-failure-count` when reliable collection is required; `retries`, `loops`, `execution-step-count`, and `execution-duration` when boundedness or timely escalation matters; `working-set-rebuild-factor` and `context-growth` when repeated context is an attention or cost risk; `trajectory-efficiency` when unnecessary tool churn is a concern; and `artifact-production` only when producing the intended artifacts is itself useful diagnostic evidence.
100	
101	Then inspect the implemented fragments in [`shared/graders/`](../workflows/shared/graders/README.md). Use `policy-near-miss` for explicit guard or no-op requirements, and `skill-constraint-coverage` when a harness/skill declares behavioral requirements that should be exercised. Use `exploration-error` when failure may stem from insufficient search, and `exploitation-error` when the agent had enough information but failed to use it. For intents that require efficient investigation rather than repeated exploration, consider `state-revisit-probability-rep`, `recurrence-rate`, `recurrence-determinism`, `recurrence-laminarity`, or `recurrence-trapping-time`. For intents where varied, non-repetitive investigation is relevant, consider `event-entropy-rate` or `lempel-ziv-trajectory-complexity`. Use `tool-output-consumption-rate` when tool outputs going unused by later actions is a risk. Import only the applicable implemented fragments and ensure their documented trace prerequisites are available. These trace graders diagnose execution behavior; they do not replace scenario evals or the operational-value attainment metric.
102	
103	## Preserve Intent on Updates
104	
105	Read the existing `intent:` before changing an existing workflow. Preserve it for an implementation-only change, including a trigger or output-channel redesign. Reconsider and update it only when the request materially expands, contracts, or otherwise changes the outcome. When it changes, re-derive conditions, architecture, prompt behavior, and evals.

127	[browser decision](playwright.md#browser-decision-and-readiness) before selecting
128	tools; add `cache-memory` only for persistent baselines or comparisons.
129	
130	## Replace Previous Results
131	
132	When a recurring digest or PR-reactive update is superseded by the newest result, prefer replacing the prior output instead of accumulating stale results:
133	
134	- For recurring issue digests, use `create-issue` with `close-older-issues: true`.
135	- For rolling PR comments, use `add-comment` with `hide-older-comments: true`.
136	
137	Wait for the previous result when only one active issue or PR should exist; keep prior outputs when each result is intentionally distinct or history is required.
138	
139	## File Format
140	
141	Agentic workflows are markdown files with YAML frontmatter.
142	
143	```markdown
144	---
145	emoji: 🧠
146	name: My Workflow
147	description: Short description
148	on:
149	  issues:
150	    types: [opened]
151	permissions:
152	  contents: read
153	  actions: read
154	strict: true
155	network:
156	  allowed: [defaults, github]
157	tools:
158	  github:
159	    mode: gh-proxy
160	    toolsets: [default]
161	safe-outputs:
162	  add-comment:
163	---
164	
165	# Workflow Title
166	
167	Natural language instructions for the AI agent.
168	```
169	
170	## Recompilation Rule
171	
172	See [workflow-editing.md](workflow-editing.md) for when `gh aw compile` is required.
173	
174	## Core Rules
175	
176	- Set `strict: true` for production workflows.
177	- Limit `bash` access to what the workflow actually needs.
178	- Keep agent-job permissions read-only when writes are handled solely by safe outputs. For example, `add-comment` needs `pull-requests: read` to inspect a PR, not `pull-requests: write`; `create-issue` needs `issues: read` to check existing issues, not `issues: write`. Safe-output writes run in separate jobs with their own permissions.
179	- For visual regression workflows, explicitly name the baseline source (for example `cache-memory` key, artifact, or branch path). See [visual-regression.md](visual-regression.md).
180	
181	See [workflow-constraints.md](workflow-constraints.md) for the security posture (read-only job, safe-outputs routing, gh-proxy/cli-proxy, network constraints, sanitized text), safer-alternatives pattern, and common risk areas.
182	
183	## Repository-Specific Instructions
184	
185	Use `@.github/aw/instructions.md` as the canonical repository-local overlay for workflow authoring standards.
186	
187	- This file is optional and repository-owned.
188	- Installed gh-aw agents should load and apply it automatically when present.
189	- Precedence: apply upstream defaults first, then apply repository overlay rules; when they conflict, repository overlay rules win.
190	
191	## Trigger Selection
192	
193	Use the smallest trigger that matches the requested automation. See the [Decision Matrix](triggers.md#decision-matrix) in triggers.md for the canonical trigger-to-use-case mapping, and [workflow-constraints.md](workflow-constraints.md) for the security posture.
194	
195	Use `pull_request` with `paths:` for checks that need only changed files. When a PR check depends on an artifact produced by another Actions workflow, use `workflow_run` scoped to that workflow with `types: [completed]` and gate on a successful conclusion, rather than racing the artifact producer on `pull_request`. Use `schedule` (with `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs) when an audit must correlate results across runs or inspect drift independently of a single PR or CI run.
196	
197	## Ad Hoc Scenario Evaluation
198	
199	For exploration/persona requests, follow
200	[ad hoc evaluation](create-agentic-workflow.md#ad-hoc-evaluation-mode).
201	Do not create/edit workflows without an explicit implementation request.
202	Address the custom agent in conversation; CLI/MCP workflow-management tools
203	do not accept freeform `prompt`, `scenario` or `query` parameters.
204	Return trigger, scope, tools, permissions, safe outputs and `noop` criteria.
205	For recurring reports, state window, grouping dimensions and a stable dedup key;
206	replace superseded digests with `create-issue.close-older-issues: true`.
207	Name design/accessibility rubrics and policy tiers when relevant; deduplicate
208	before escalating compliance findings.
209	
210	## PR Checks with Linked References
211	
212	Read PR-body/comment references with `gh pr view`; verify access and content
213	before assessing compliance. Use `add-comment` for satisfied requirements,
214	specific gaps or missing links; escalate via `create-issue` only when policy
215	requires it. Call `noop` for out-of-scope PRs. Keep agent permissions read-only.
216	Use [compliance guidance](create-agentic-workflow-trigger-details.md#compliance-review-guidance)
217	for license tiers, path scope and escalation.

264	
265	# Agentic Workflow Constraints
266	
267	## Execution Model
268	
269	Agentic workflows run as a **single GitHub Actions job** with one agent execution.
270	
271	## Can Do
272	
273	- read GitHub data, APIs, web pages, and local repository files
274	- run tools inside the single job
275	- use MCP servers and safe outputs
276	- create GitHub resources through `safe-outputs:`
277	- persist lightweight state with `cache-memory` or other approved mechanisms
278	
279	## Cannot Do
280	
281	- pause and resume for external events
282	- orchestrate multi-stage pipelines with job dependencies
283	- pass state between multiple AI jobs in one workflow run
284	- implement built-in rollback across external systems
285	- wait for another workflow or deployment to finish inside the same agent run
286	
287	## Recommend Traditional GitHub Actions When
288	
289	- multi-stage deployment pipelines
290	- fan-out/fan-in job orchestration
291	- long waits for approvals or external systems
292	- rollback logic across several steps or systems
293	- cross-job state transfer
294	
295	Suggested response:
296	
297	> This requires capabilities the single-job agentic model does not support. Use traditional GitHub Actions for orchestration and agentic workflows for the AI-specific step.
298	
299	## Security Posture
300	
301	- Keep the main agent job read-only.
302	- Do not add GitHub write permissions to the agent job.
303	- Route GitHub writes through `safe-outputs:`.
304	- Do not create issues directly through agent tools, `gh`, or GitHub APIs; use `safe-outputs.create-issue`, check for an existing issue first, and use `noop` when no issue is needed.
305	- Prefer `tools.github.mode: gh-proxy` with `gh` for GitHub reads.
306	- Prefer `tools.cli-proxy: true` with mounted `mcp-clis` commands for non-GitHub MCP tools.
307	- Constrain `network.allowed:` to the minimum required ecosystems or domains.
308	- For workflows that only inspect in-repo files and/or read GitHub through `gh-proxy`, default to no network access (`network.allowed: []`), not `network: defaults`. Allow `defaults` when infrastructure access is needed for install/build/test steps, alongside the required ecosystem for package downloads.
309	- Use `${{ steps.sanitized.outputs.text }}` for untrusted user content.
310	- Never pass `${{ secrets.* }}` or other credentials to `post-steps:` or custom secret-scanning steps, or write secret values to logs or artifacts. Use supported declarative authentication for agent tools, or run credential-dependent scanning in a separate least-privilege non-agent job without exposing secret values.
311	
312	## Safer Alternatives First
313	
314	When a requested feature increases risk:
315	
316	1. explain the risk
317	2. propose the safer pattern first
318	3. require explicit confirmation before relaxing safeguards
319	
320	## Common Risk Areas
321	
322	- direct write permissions instead of safe outputs
323	- auto-merge or bypassing review
324	- overly broad network access
325	- unbounded bash allowlists for untrusted input
326	- shell injection: interpolating `${{ github.event.* }}` or other untrusted expressions directly into `run:` scripts; pass untrusted values through environment variables instead
327	- placing OIDC/secret bootstrap in `pre-steps` instead of earlier `setup-steps`
328	- using `post-steps:` for agent-driven write actions
329	- placing credentials in `post-steps:` or custom secret-scanning steps
330	
331	## Self-Hosted Runner Compatibility
332	
333	When `runs-on` is any value other than GitHub-hosted labels (`ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-slim`, `windows-latest`, `macos-latest`):
334	
335	- Set `runs-on` explicitly (not inherited from imports); accepts string, array, or runner-group object. Framework jobs (activation, safe-outputs, unlock, etc.) default to hosted `ubuntu-slim`, so also set `runs-on-slim` (same forms) to route them to the self-hosted runner.
336	- Write transient state, tool downloads, and outputs under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, not `/tmp` (which can persist across jobs on shared runners).
337	- Agent steps run as the runner user, not root — don't install to system-wide paths. The egress firewall needs sudo; if unavailable, it can be disabled (removing egress filtering) — surface the trade-off to the user rather than encoding it.
338	- Declare every outbound domain in `network.allowed`; `defaults` covers only certificate, JSON-schema, and stock Ubuntu hosts, so add `github`, language ecosystems, or engine sets explicitly (see [network.md](network.md)). Non-allow-listed domains are blocked when the firewall is enabled.
339	- Do not install to `/usr/local` or the toolcache (may be read-only/shared); use job-scoped writable paths.
340	- Do not hardcode `/home/runner` or any literal home path — read `$HOME`; use `$RUNNER_TEMP` for transient state.
341	- For GitHub Enterprise Server, enable GHES compatibility (GHES-compatible artifact action versions, enterprise API endpoint).
342	
343	For the full set of requirements (Docker socket, ARC / Docker-in-Docker, network egress, GHES specifics), follow the [Self-Hosted Runners](/gh-aw/reference/self-hosted-runners/) reference page.
344	
345	## Shared Reminder
346	
347	Reference this file from creator, updater, and debugger prompts instead of repeating the architectural explanation.
